title: Flood Fill
signature: floodFill(image: List[List[int]], sr: int, sc: int, color: int) -> List[List[int]]
statement: Starting at pixel (sr, sc), recolour that pixel and every pixel connected to it horizontally or vertically that has the same ORIGINAL colour, with the new colour. Return the image.

large_tests.gen_code:
def gen():
    return [[[0] * 300 for _ in range(300)], 150, 150, 5]

hints.1_question: Which pixels change? Only those connected to the start through pixels of the starting colour. What if the new colour equals the old one?
hints.2_nudge: Explore from the start with a stack/queue, recolouring pixels with the original colour. If original == new colour, return immediately.
hints.3_big_hint: if image[sr][sc] == color: return image. Else flood fill 4 directions over cells whose colour == orig.

known_bugs.name: loops forever when the new colour equals the old colour
known_bugs.followup: If the new colour equals the old colour, how do you tell a pixel you've already visited from one you haven't?

known_bugs.name: fills diagonal neighbours too
known_bugs.followup: Which neighbours count as connected for flood fill?

known_bugs.name: recursive version (recursion limit)
known_bugs.followup: How deep can the recursion get when 90000 pixels share one colour?
